input.question: Why is it when we look back at things in our past they seem a lot better than they actually are?
input.ground_truth: Because you remember the best, eventful memories in more detail. You tend to block out all the normal things like changing you socks or taking a shit that day. Similar to when you zone out in the shower trying to think if you've just washed your hair or not. You do those things everyday and block them out of memory.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why is it when we look back at things in our past they seem a lot better than they actually are?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy that you really, really liked when you were little. Now, when you look at a picture of that toy or remember playing with it, you think, “Wow, that was the best toy ever!” But if you actually find the toy now, it might be broken, missing a piece, or not as fun as you remember.

That’s because your brain likes to remember the happy parts and forgets the not-so-good parts. When you think about the past, you mostly remember how happy and fun things were, not the boring or sad parts. So, things from the past seem better in your memory than they really were.
